historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr, rounded down. Equity CAGR is unusable as the anchor: $6.5B of FY2021-22 buybacks and the FY2023 East Palestine charge ($1.1B pre-tax) drove book value, not earnings power. FCF CAGRs are flat because FY2020 was a capex trough (1,494) and FY2025 carries elevated capex plus settlement outflows.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 1.0% vs revenue 4.5% and EPS 10.1% (>30% divergence). Cause: buybacks (FY2021 $3.4B, FY2022 $3.1B) and the FY2023 derailment charge, not a shrinking business. EPS 5-yr CAGR is flattered by the FY2020 pandemic trough base. 3-yr CAGRs are negative because FY2022 was the fuel-surcharge peak.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (no interest-income strip, net debt company). SBC is 0.3-0.5% of revenue throughout, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs barely differ; SBC is not where this valuation's risk lives. The FCF history is the story of capex intensity (18-20% of revenue since FY2023 vs 15% in FY2020-21) and East Palestine cash costs.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone NSC executes PSR 2.0 roughly as guided: after a fuel-surcharge-driven +10.5% in FY2026, revenue grows 3-4% nominal, adjusted operating ratio improves about a point a year from 66.4% (nine months 2026) to the low-60s, capex holds near $2.1-2.3B. The three axes are (1) OR progression vs the mid-60s guidance, (2) intermodal and merchandise volume vs US industrial production, and (3) capex intensity, which is what separates rail EBITDA from rail FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Standalone upside: volume growth from truck conversion and reshoring, OR to the ~60% peer frontier, capex intensity easing. This is the ceiling for NSC on its own; it is still well below the UP consideration, which is why the deal, not operations, is the bull case the market is actually pricing.
scenario_narratives.bear: The STB blocks or conditions the merger into abandonment during 2027 -- a path made more visible since October by the board's inquiry into the UP chief executive's remarks to shippers, CPKC's motion to terminate the proceeding, and opposition filings from five state attorneys general and a bipartisan group of senators. NSC emerges with two years of deferred decisions, some customer and crew attrition, an industrial slowdown, and OR stuck near 67%. The stock loses the deal premium and re-rates toward standalone fundamentals; the $2.5B termination fee (~$11/share, confirmed in the Q3 2026 10-Q note 1) is the only cushion.

deal_overlay.status: Pending acquisition by Union Pacific (merger agreement 2025-07-28; shareholders approved; STB review live). The STB restarted the review and set its procedural schedule in August 2026 and moved to merits evaluation on 2026-09-01; opposition comments were due 2026-11-18. Since the prior valuation: an STB judge ordered public a video of UP's chief executive telling shippers he would raise rates on merger opponents, the board opened an inquiry into shipper intimidation and reopened participation, CPKC moved to terminate the proceeding, and five state attorneys general, a bipartisan group of senators and farm groups filed against the deal; Schneider filed in support. Source for these events: news headlines dated 2026-10-25 to 2026-11-19 (Railway Age, Trains, FreightWaves, Business Journals) -- headline-level only, not read against the STB docket. Final-decision timing is carried from the prior version (2027); not re-verified.
deal_overlay.consideration: 1.0 UNP share + $88.82 cash per NSC share
deal_overlay.unp_price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:03Z regular close, Yahoo Finance chart API
deal_overlay.expected_close: 2027, after the STB's final decision; NSC keeps paying its $1.35 quarterly dividend while pending.
deal_overlay.reverse_termination_fee: $2.5B payable by either party under specified circumstances (Q3 2026 10-Q note 1) = $11.10/share on 225.2M diluted shares. Treated as received by NSC on a regulatory failure; the precise triggers are in the merger agreement (8-K of 2025-07-29, exhibit 2.1) and were not re-read.
deal_overlay.probability_rationale: Cut from 0.60 to 0.55. The structural case is as before: a first-of-its-kind transcontinental Class I merger under the STB's 2001 'enhance competition' standard, with every other Class I and the main shipper associations opposed, but with commitments that make approval-with-conditions plausible. What moved it: the record now contains the acquirer's chief executive threatening shippers who oppose the deal, the board has opened an inquiry on it, and the political opposition has broadened to state attorneys general and senators of both parties. The market agrees in direction: NSC's discount to the consideration widened from 14.1% to 17.0% while UNP rose 10%. It is a five-point cut and not more because the evidence is headline-level and the STB has not ruled on any of the motions.
deal_overlay.deal_weighted_method: 0.55 x 389.72 (consideration at UNP 300.90) + 0.45 x 173.39 (standalone weighted IV + termination fee) = 292.37. Consideration is NOT discounted for time because the $5.40/yr dividend collected while pending roughly offsets the carry.
deal_overlay.market_implied_probability_note: (323.50 - 173.39) / (389.72 - 173.39) = 69% against the DCF break value; (323.50 - 245) / (389.72 - 245) = 54% against a pre-deal-band break value. The house 55% sits at the lower reading.
deal_overlay.break_value_note: Standalone weighted IV 162.29 + 11.10 termination fee. A market re-rate on a break would more likely land in the pre-announcement trading band (~$230-250, June 2025, ~20x earnings) than at the DCF value; both readings are given. The pre-deal band has not been adjusted for the ~60bp rise in the 10-year yield since June 2025.
deal_overlay.deal_weighted_value_if_break_rerates_not: 0.55 x 389.72 + 0.45 x 245 (midpoint of the pre-announcement band) = 324.60; this is roughly where the stock trades, i.e. the market is using a peer-multiple fallback, not an owner-FCF fallback.
deal_overlay.reading: The stock offers ~$66 (20%) of upside if the deal closes at UNP's current price and ~$78-150 of downside if it breaks (to the pre-deal band or to the DCF break value respectively). On the house 55% probability the expected value (~$292) is BELOW the price on the DCF fallback and roughly AT the price on a peer-multiple fallback. There is no margin of safety for a fundamental buyer at this level; this is a merger-arbitrage position whose return depends on the STB and on UNP's share price, not on NSC's cash flows.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Two valuations, kept apart on purpose. (1) The standalone owner-FCF DCF -- three scenarios, 10-year component build, 9.0% WACC, terminal capped at 14-18x owner FCF -- is the fundamental anchor: what NSC is worth as an eastern Class I railroad with 17-18% capex intensity and a mid-60s operating ratio. (2) The pending Union Pacific acquisition is the dominant near-term price driver and is handled as a deal overlay, not as a growth scenario: the consideration (1.0 UNP + $88.82) is a function of UNP's share price and STB approval odds, neither of which is a driver path. The market price sits between the standalone value and the consideration; where it sits is a statement about deal probability, not about NSC's cash flows. Deal completion caps upside at the consideration; a deal break re-rates the stock toward the standalone band, cushioned only by the reverse termination fee and the dividend collected while waiting.
valuation_philosophy.what_the_dcf_says: Standalone, the stock is worth materially less than the current price on every scenario, including the bull case. That is not unusual for a Class I railroad: the market pays 20-25x earnings for pricing power and network scarcity that an owner-FCF model, which charges the full 17-18% capex burden every year, does not credit. Pre-announcement (June 2025) NSC traded in the $230-250 range; the DCF range below that reflects the house 16x owner-FCF terminal cap and the full capex charge.
key_risks_to_valuation: STB outcome is binary and dominates the 12-month return: approval -> consideration (~$390 at UNP's current price, itself volatile); block/abandonment -> re-rate toward standalone, a 25-50% drawdown from the current price depending on whether the market falls back to a peer multiple or to owner-FCF value.

UNP share price: each $10 move in UNP moves the consideration $10/share; the stock component is unhedged for a plain holder. UNP has risen ~10% since the prior valuation, which is most of the reason NSC is up.
Discount rate: the 10-year Treasury is ~5.1%. Base value is ~$165 at 9.0% and was ~$184 on the same drivers at 8.0%; a point of WACC is worth roughly $20/share.

Fuel surcharge: ~$720M of FY2026's revenue increase is fuel surcharge. The model holds revenue at that level and rebases capex and D&A percentages to it; a fuel-price reversal cuts revenue ~5% with little EBITDA effect, but anyone moving the growth slider alone will overstate the damage.

Operating ratio execution: every point of OR is ~$135M of EBIT; the base case assumes ~2.5 points of margin improvement over five years that NSC has guided toward but not delivered -- nine-month 2026 adjusted OR was 66.4% against 64.8% a year earlier.
Capex intensity: the base case holds capex near $2.1-2.3B; a return to the $2.3-2.4B of FY2023-24 without matching revenue takes roughly $10-15/share off the standalone value.
Cash tax rate: the model keeps cash tax below book (15% -> 19%) on permanent bonus depreciation; a legislative reversal would push the rate to 21% from year one.
East Palestine tail: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow fell $578M on Incident payments and a further $53M was expensed; modelled as zero further cash cost beyond the 2026-09-30 balance sheet.
Cyclicality: merchandise and intermodal volumes track US industrial production; a recession in the review window hits both the standalone value and, through UNP's price, the consideration.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back ($63M). NSC does not tag PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation separately; withholding is immaterial at SBC of 0.5% of revenue and is not added.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow $534M (XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock). Nothing repurchased in the first nine months of 2026: the merger agreement prohibits repurchases without Union Pacific's consent (Q3 2026 10-Q; $6.3B of authorisation unused). The flat share count is a modelling convention funded historically (FY2021-22 $6.5B of buybacks) but currently suspended under the deal.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted weighted-average Q3 2026 10-Q (225.2M; basic 224.6M; cover page 224,616,686 at 2026-09-30); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 5.07% (10y UST, ^TNX close 2026-11-18; it has been 4.9-5.3% since mid-September), ERP 4.5%, beta ~1.1 (pre-deal rail beta; the merger-arb regime has collapsed observed beta and is not used) -> cost of equity ~10.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6.2% (BBB+/Baa1 spread ~115bp over the 10y), 21% tax -> ~4.9% after tax. Market-value weights ~81% equity / 19% debt (market cap ~$73B vs $16.6B debt) -> 9.05%, used as 9.0%. CORRECTION vs the 2026-10-02 version: that build used 8.0% on a stated Rf of 4.1%, but the 10y was already ~5.2% on that date -- the risk-free input was stale, not a judgment. Same WACC on all three scenarios: cyclicality and deal-break risk are charged in the flows and the weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: ASC 842 operating leases ($218M liability at FY2025; ~$92M/yr lease cost) are expensed inside operating expenses, so EBITDA is already after the lease charge; operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt (treatment B, charged once). The April 2026 headquarters finance lease ($115M liability, replacing an operating lease) sits inside reported long-term debt and is therefore in net debt; its cost has left operating expense for depreciation and interest, so it is also charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest. Equity-method earnings (Conrail etc.) sit in other income and are left out of EBITDA; the stakes are not added to the bridge either, so nothing is counted twice.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income is not separately tagged after FY2017 (sits inside OtherNonoperatingIncomeExpense, $101M FY2025 net). Not stripped: NSC is net DEBT $15.5B, so the cash pile is not being added to EV and there is nothing to double-count.
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY2025 cash taxes paid $491M against pre-tax income $3,665M (13.4%) and book tax $792M (21.6%); deferred tax expense $277M. Grossing the interest shield back onto the unlevered base gives ~15% on EBIT. Bonus depreciation (made permanent by the 2025 tax act) keeps the cash rate below book as long as capex exceeds D&A, which is structural for a railroad, so the ramp only goes to 19% not 21%. Unchanged in this update: the Q3 2026 10-Q gives no cash-tax disclosure that moves it.
inputs.debt_note: Q3 2026 10-Q balance sheet (2026-09-30): long-term debt $15,964M + current maturities $649M = $16,613M (fair-value note: 'Long-term debt, including current maturities (16,613)'); cash and equivalents $1,598M. Net debt $15,015M, down $532M from 2026-06-30 as buybacks are suspended and cash accumulates. Debt-to-total-capitalisation 49.8%.
inputs.notes: UPDATE of the 2026-10-02 valuation, not a rebuild; see reconciliation and unchanged_assumptions. Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md row: operating company, cyclical US industrial; owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md rules b and f) -- same model as the prior version. The SKILL.md 'live takeover' row also applies: the pending Union Pacific acquisition is still live (STB merits review; opposition comments closed 2026-11-18) and is weighted deal-completes vs deal-breaks in deal_overlay, NOT inside the three scenarios, because a stock-and-cash consideration is not a driver path. The canonical weighted_iv is therefore the STANDALONE value, i.e. what the equity is worth if the deal breaks, before the termination fee; the deal-weighted value is deal_overlay.deal_weighted_value_per_share. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue $12,180M). Year 1 = FY2026, now anchored to nine months of actuals plus guidance: revenue ~+10.5% (roughly 6 points of it fuel surcharge), EBITDA margin 45.0% before SBC (= adjusted operating margin 33.6% + depreciation 10.7% + SBC 0.7%; merger-related and Eastern Ohio costs excluded as non-recurring on a standalone view), capex $2.1B as guided. Because fuel surcharge lifts revenue without lifting capital needs, capex and D&A percentages from year 2 are rebased down by the same ~5% so that capex DOLLARS match the prior path; if fuel prices fall back, revenue falls, the EBITDA margin rises and those percentages must be rebased up again -- roughly value-neutral, but the paths are not independent. Year-1 owner-FCF cross-check: engine ~$3.2B unlevered vs FY2026E actual of ~$2.3B (OCF ~3,870 + after-tax interest ~620 - capex 2,100 - SBC ~95); the ~$0.9B gap is Incident settlement cash (~$0.6B, the stated cause of the nine-month OCF decline) plus merger costs, most of it already paid and therefore already inside the 2026-09-30 net debt. Merger-related expense (~$190M/yr while pending) is not charged in the flows: ~$1-2/share if the deal runs through 2027. Price is a regular close, not after-hours. Band position: house and street IVs are a few dollars apart because SBC is 0.5-0.7% of revenue, and the price sits far above BOTH; the engine's band_position is a degenerate reading of a tiny band, not a statement about SBC accounting -- the gap between price and both IVs is the merger premium plus the market's peer-multiple fallback, see deal_overlay.
inputs.fy2026_run_rate_note: Nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q): revenue $9,989M (+9%; Q3 $3,526M, +14%), adjusted income from railway operations $3,355M, adjusted OR 66.4% (Q3 65.4%; GAAP 68.5% / 67.4% after $145M merger-related expense and $53M Eastern Ohio cost), depreciation $1,073M (10.7% of revenue), SBC $72M (0.72%), OCF $2,720M (down from $3,298M on Incident cash payments), property additions $1,407M with FY2026 guided to ~$2.1B. Fuel surcharge revenue $1.1B vs $613M: $480M of the $783M nine-month revenue increase is fuel surcharge, $189M volume (+2% units), $114M rate/mix. Ex-fuel-surcharge growth is ~3.3%.

bear.narrative: Deal is blocked or abandoned in 2027 after two years of strategic limbo: FY2026 still lands at ~+10% (nine months are in), then customer-contract and employee attrition, a mild industrial recession in 2027, coal decline and truck competition on intermodal hold volume flat; OR stalls at 67-68% (EBITDA margin ~44.5%); capex stays elevated under heightened FRA/safety scrutiny (prior 18.5% in dollars, 17.3% of the fuel-inflated revenue); cash tax normalises to 21%. 14x terminal cap binds (Gordon 14.6x). Tax is never credited on a loss, EBIT stays positive throughout, and the terminal value does not hit the zero floor.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +10.5% (nine months +9%, Q3 +14%; ~6 points is fuel surcharge, underlying ~3.3%), then the prior path: 4% fading to 2.5% nominal, which assumes fuel surcharge holds at the current level. EBITDA margin 45.0% in FY2026 (nine-month adjusted OR 66.4%) improving about half a point a year to 47.5% as PSR 2.0 delivers, then holds. Capex $2.1B in FY2026 as guided (15.6% of the fuel-inflated revenue), then 16.6% -> 16.2% (the prior 17.5% -> 17.0% in dollars); D&A 10.5%. Cash tax ramps 15% -> 19%. Terminal: Gordon (9.0% / 2.5% = 15.8x) now binds just below the 16x cap.

bull.narrative: Standalone best case, not the deal: FY2026 +11%, then intermodal truck-to-rail conversion (domestic intermodal units +10% in Q3 2026) and reshoring-led merchandise growth keep volume growth at 2-3% on top of 3% pricing; OR reaches CSX/UP-class ~59-60% (EBITDA margin 50%) by year 7; capex intensity eases as the post-derailment safety catch-up completes (prior 17.5% -> 16% path, rebased to 16.2% -> 15.3% on the fuel-inflated revenue). Terminal: Gordon (9.0% / 3.0% = 17.2x) binds below the 18x cap.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: These weight the STANDALONE scenarios; deal-completes vs deal-breaks is weighted separately in deal_overlay. Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the standalone future only becomes relevant if the deal fails, and a failed deal arrives with limbo damage (attrition, deferred capital decisions) that the base case does not carry. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (OR to ~60%, sustained volume growth, lower capex intensity) and NSC has trailed peers on OR execution for a decade.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
